# Action reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-action-reference.mjs in the cellucid repository from the action
     catalog (assets/js/app/actions/definitions/). Do not edit: run that script.
     tests/action-reference-contract.test.mjs fails while this page differs from what it writes. -->

This page answers: **"What can be done to an open dataset, by name, and what does each step
change?"** Every change a person makes with a control, and every change or read an agent,
a Python or R viewer, a session or a replay makes, is one of these actions, checked
against the same parameters and recorded as one history step with the same label. The
catalog is `assets/js/app/actions/definitions/` in the `cellucid` repository
(`app/actions/README.md` there); this page is generated from it. How the action layer, the
state domains and the history work is {doc}`29_action_layer_domains_and_history`.

The catalog holds 189 actions: 103 that change the state or open a dataset, 2 that stop work under way, 37 that move or edit the history, 13 that act outside the state (a file written, a publication, what this browser keeps), and 34 reads.
Parameters name things, never positions: a field as `{source, key}` (`obs` for a column of
the cells, `var` for a gene), a category by its label, a gene by its name, a highlight page
by its name, a view as `"live"` or `"View N"`, and cells by their original position (the
0-based row of `obs`). A step therefore replays on another dataset with the same names. An
agent calls an action by its tool name (the type with dots and dashes as underscores).

## State domains

An action names the parts of the state it changes ("Changes"). The history keeps their values
before and after each step; undo puts the before-values back. It also names the parts its
result depends on besides its parameters ("Depends on": the cells, mapping or pages it computes
from, the state a name it is given resolves in); a step keeps their value hashes, which say
when its result is stale.

| Domain | Name | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `cells` | Open cells | Which cells are open (every cell, or a subsample) and how many of them genes are read for. |
| `mapping` | Data mapping | Which stored arrays are plotted and read (the data mapping). |
| `expression` | Expression values | The values the genes are shown and analyzed in: normalized to 10,000 counts per cell, log1p, or as stored. |
| `field-overlays` | Fields and labels | Field and category renames, deleted fields, user-defined fields with their values. |
| `gene-sets` | Gene sets | Gene sets pushed by a notebook or made in the app. |
| `views` | Views | Kept views, their layout, the focused view, camera lock, the representation each view shows. |
| `active-field` | Active field | What each view is colored by (a field or a gene). |
| `filters` | Filters | Category visibility, continuous ranges, outlier and missing-value filters, per view. |
| `colors` | Colors | Category colors, color maps, color ranges, log scale, zero gray, per view. |
| `visibility` | Hidden cells | Cells hidden one by one (the cell visibility mask), per view. |
| `highlights` | Highlights | Highlight pages and their groups of cells. |
| `camera` | Camera | The camera of each view and the navigation mode. |
| `camera-path` | Camera path | Camera path keyframes and their playback settings. |
| `settings` | Settings | Render, navigation and overlay settings (every stable control of the sidebar). |
| `analysis` | Analysis | The analyses of the panel and of each window: their settings and results. |
| `layout` | Layout | Docked and floating panels, analysis windows' places and sizes, open sections, sidebar, theme. |

## History

### `history.anndata.save`

**Save AnnData with this state.** Write a new Cellucid-ready AnnData file (.zarr.zip) of the whole open dataset with the state shown applied, as Python and R apply a session: renamed labels, user-defined fields and highlight groups as obs columns, gene sets in uns and var, and a record of what was applied; never over the dataset's own file.

- Agent tool: `history_anndata_save`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it writes a file (`writes-file`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | no | The new file's name (.zarr.zip is added when it does not end so); "&lt;dataset> with this state.zarr.zip" when left out. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | The file's name. |
| `to` | one of `"file"`, `"download"` | file: a file the person chose in the save dialog; download: the browser's downloads. |
| `bytes` | integer |  |
| `layout` | one of `"anndata"`, `"mudata"` | A Cellucid-ready AnnData, or a MuData for a dataset of several modalities. |
| `cells` | integer | Cells written: every cell of the dataset, whichever were open. |
| `tracker` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `branch` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `step` | string | The step applied: the one shown. |
| `applied` | boolean | False when every change was in the dataset already (no record added). |
| `rows` | list of object (`kind`, `name`, `status`, `cells`, `note`) | Every change of the apply plan, in domain order, as Python and R plan it. |
| `left_out` | list of string | What the copy does not hold of the state, or of the dataset, one sentence each. |

Timeline label: Saved an AnnData copy with this state

Pseudocode: `save_anndata()`

### `history.bookmark.set`

**Bookmark a step.** Give a step a bookmark name, unique in its tracker (jump to it by name), or remove it with null. Bookmark before destructive or heavy work.

- Agent tool: `history_bookmark_set`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step` | string | yes | A step of the tracker in use, by its id (history_get lists the steps). |
| `name` | string or null | yes | The bookmark, or null to remove it. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"step":"s3","name":"Before reclustering"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `step` | string |  |
| `bookmark` | string or null |  |
| `journal` | string |  |

Timeline label: Bookmarked step 3 as "Before reclustering"

Pseudocode: `bookmark("s3", "Before reclustering")`

### `history.branch.apply`

**Apply a branch's steps here.** Apply a branch's own steps again, by name, on top of the step shown, as a new branch (no values are merged; a step that does not apply here is flagged).

- Agent tool: `history_branch_apply`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `branch` | string | yes | A branch by its name or its id (history_summary lists them). Not empty. |
| `name` | string | no | A name, unique among its kind (compared without case and extra spaces); no length limit. Not empty. |
| `tracker` | string | no | A tracker by its name or its id (history_summary lists them); the tracker in use when left out. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"branch":"Main"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `branch` | object (`id`, `name`) or null |  |
| `head` | string | The step shown now. |
| `report` | list of object (`source`, `label`, `outcome`, `step`, `reason`, `missing`) | Every step replayed and what became of it. |

Timeline label: Applied the steps of branch "Main" here

Pseudocode: `apply_branch(branch="Main")`

### `history.branch.delete`

**Delete a branch.** Move a branch's own steps (those no other branch starts from) to Recently deleted, where they can be restored; with with_sub_branches, the branches that start from it too. Main and locked branches cannot be deleted.

- Agent tool: `history_branch_delete`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it deletes something saved (`deletes-saved`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `branch` | string | yes | A branch by its name or its id (history_summary lists them). Not empty. |
| `with_sub_branches` | boolean | no | Also delete every branch that starts from it. Default `false`. |
| `tracker` | string | no | A tracker by its name or its id (history_summary lists them); the tracker in use when left out. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"branch":"Main"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `branches` | list of object (`id`, `name`) | The branches deleted. |
| `steps` | integer | Steps moved to Recently deleted. |
| `results` | integer | Results computed on them. |
| `kept_views` | integer | Kept views elsewhere made from it (they keep their picture). |
| `replays` | integer | Trackers replayed from it. |
| `absorbed_by` | object (`id`, `name`) or null | The branch that keeps its shared steps. |
| `head` | string | The step shown now. |
| `journal` | string | Its Recently deleted entry. |

Timeline label: Deleted branch "Main"

Pseudocode: `delete_branch(branch="Main")`

### `history.clear`

**Clear the history.** Start the branch "Fresh start" from the opening step with nothing behind it: keeping the state shown (one squashed step from the dataset as opened to it), or from the dataset as opened (the branch starts with the next change). Every branch stays, archivable; either way it is kept in Recently changed and can be undone there.

- Agent tool: `history_clear`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it deletes something saved (`deletes-saved`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keep_state` | boolean | yes | True keeps the state shown as one step; false starts over from the dataset as opened. |

Example:

```json
{"keep_state":true}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `branch` | object (`id`, `name`) or null |  |
| `head` | string | The step shown now. |
| `journal` | string | Its Recently changed entry. |

Timeline label: Cleared the history, keeping the state

Pseudocode: `clear_history(keep_state=True)`

### `history.diff`

**Compare two steps.** What differs between the state after two steps, part by part (filters, labels, highlights, …); the steps may be of two trackers.

- Agent tool: `history_diff`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a` | object (`step`, `tracker`) | yes | The first step. |
| `b` | object (`step`, `tracker`) | yes | The second step. |

Example:

```json
{"a":{"step":"s1"},"b":{"step":"s2"}}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | object (`tracker`, `step`) |  |
| `b` | object (`tracker`, `step`) |  |
| `common` | string or null | Their last common step (null across trackers). |
| `domains` | list of object (`domain`, `name`, `lines`) |  |

### `history.get`

**Read the history.** The steps taken on this dataset, who took each (person, agent, notebook), branches and the step shown.

- Agent tool: `history_get`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracker` | string | no | A tracker by its name or its id (history_summary lists them); the tracker in use when left out. Not empty. |
| `branch` | string | no | The path to this branch's tip (by its name or id) instead of the path to the step shown; not with all_branches. Not empty. |
| `all_branches` | boolean | no | Every branch, not only the path to the step shown. Default `false`. |
| `since` | number | no | Only the steps recorded at or after this time (milliseconds since 1970: a step's "at"), so a second read lists what came since. |
| `limit` | integer | no | The steps of one page (200 when left out: well under what a tool result carries). At least 1. Default `200`. |
| `cursor` | string | no | Where the page starts: the next of the last page (its last step's id); the first page when left out. Not empty. |
| `fields` | list of one of `"params"`, `"notes"`, `"bookmark"` | no | What to add to each step: params (each parameter in words), notes, bookmark. Each once. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tracker` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `trackers` | list of object (`id`, `name`, `active`) |  |
| `head` | string | The step shown now. |
| `branches` | list of object (`name`, `tip`, `active`) |  |
| `steps` | list of object (`id`, `parent`, `kind`, `squash`, `label`, `type`, `v`, `code`, `origin`, `agent`, `host`, `turn`, `at`, `status`, `note`, `touches`, `group`, `shown`, `params`, `notes`, `bookmark`) | One page: root first; parents before children. |
| `total` | integer | Steps on every page (the path to the step shown, or every branch). |
| `next` | string or null | The cursor of the next page; null on the last. |

- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)

| `to` | string | yes | Its last step. |
| `name` | string | yes | A name, unique among its kind (compared without case and extra spaces); no length limit. Not empty. |

Example:


It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `group` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `steps` | integer | Steps in it. |
| `journal` | string | Its Recently changed entry. |

Timeline label: Grouped steps 4 to 9 as "QC"

### `history.journal.undo`

**Restore from Recently deleted.** Undo an edit of the history (a delete, a rename, a note, …) from Recently deleted: exactly as it was when nothing changed it since, else as new objects ("X (restored)", removed steps applied again as a branch). Undoing a rename whose old name was taken since is refused, naming the name to use instead.

- Agent tool: `history_journal_undo`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entry` | string | yes | An entry of Recently deleted, by its id (history_summary counts them). |
| `tracker` | string | no | A tracker by its name or its id (history_summary lists them); the tracker in use when left out. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"entry":"j0"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `entry` | string |  |
| `restored` | one of `"exact"`, `"as-new"` |  |
| `journal` | string | The entry the restore itself made (undoable). |
| `branch` | object (`id`, `name`) or null | The first branch a restore as new made of the steps it applied again. |

### `history.saved.open`

**Open a saved state.** Open one saved state of this browser (by its id from history_saved_list) to continue it, as Load…'s Open does: its dataset first when another is shown (with the cells it was saved on), then its history, which goes on where it left off (an autosave keeps being written; a named save stays as it was and the history goes on as a new autosave). The history shown before stays kept in this browser while Autosave keeps it (steps it does not keep are asked about first). To apply its steps to the dataset shown instead, use history_replay. A whole-file download is asked about first.

- Agent tool: `history_saved_open`
- Effect: `dataset`: it opens another dataset, whose history starts anew (the open one's stays kept in this browser while Autosave keeps it), and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it downloads a lot (`large-download`)
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it while the dataset shown holds steps this browser is not keeping (Autosave off, no storage or no room), which it would drop (`replaces-unkept`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `saved` | string | yes | Its id (history_saved_list). Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"saved":"state-1"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `saved` | string |  |
| `name` | string or null | Its name; null for an autosave. |
| `dataset` | string or null | The name of its dataset, now open. |
| `steps` | integer |  |
| `dataset_opened` | boolean | Its dataset was opened first (another one was shown). |
| `already_shown` | boolean | It is the history shown already, which goes on; nothing was opened. |
| `not_restored` | string or null | Null when every part was restored. Otherwise each part that could not be (a state domain such as the Expression values, a tracker's steps), one sentence each, as the person was told: that part is left as it was shown (a part saved by another version of Cellucid that this one cannot read says so), the rest is restored, and the saved state is kept as it was while the history goes on beside it. |

Timeline label: Opened the saved state state-1

Pseudocode: `history_saved_open("state-1")`

### `history.step.revert`

**Revert a step.** Add a step that puts back exactly what a step changed, when no later step on the path changed the same parts (else use Branch without a step).

- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Open cells (`cells`), Data mapping (`mapping`), Expression values (`expression`), Fields and labels (`field-overlays`), Gene sets (`gene-sets`), Views (`views`), Active field (`active-field`), Filters (`filters`), Colors (`colors`), Hidden cells (`visibility`), Highlights (`highlights`), Camera (`camera`), Camera path (`camera-path`), Settings (`settings`), Analysis (`analysis`), Layout (`layout`)

|---|---|---|---|

### `history.summary`

**Summarize the history.** The history at a glance: trackers, branches (fork step, tip, steps, main, locked, archived), bookmarks, turns, stale results and Recently deleted, without the steps; the notes on the tracker, each branch, group and turn in full (a shared session's notes are its sender's account). Read it before acting on the history.

- Agent tool: `history_summary`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracker` | string | no | A tracker by its name or its id (history_summary lists them); the tracker in use when left out. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tracker` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `notes` | list of object (`id`, `text`, `by`, `at`, `edited_at`, `from_reply`) | The notes on the tracker itself (the methods paragraph's opening). |
| `trackers` | list of object (`id`, `name`, `active`, `steps`, `start`) | Every tracker not removed. |
| `head` | string | The step shown now. |
| `active_branch` | string |  |
| `main_branch` | string |  |
| `recording` | object (`on`, `since`) |  |
| `pending` | object (`name`, `from`) or null |  |
| `steps` | integer | Steps of the tracker, the root included. |
| `branches` | list of object (`id`, `name`, `base`, `tip`, `steps`, `main`, `locked`, `archived`, `active`, `notes`) | Every branch, in id order (archived ones flagged). |
| `groups` | list of object (`id`, `name`, `branch`, `first`, `last`, `steps`, `notes`) | Every group, in id order: a named run of consecutive steps of one branch. |
| `bookmarks` | list of object (`name`, `step`) |  |
| `turns` | list of object (`id`, `label`, `by`, `steps`, `branch`, `notes`) |  |
| `stale` | integer | Results whose inputs changed since (history_stale lists them). |
| `recently_deleted` | integer | Entries that can be undone. |

## Fields

### `category.delete`

**Delete a category.** Move every cell of one category into the Unassigned category. A column from the file becomes a new column (the original moves to Deleted fields); a column made in the app is edited in place.

- Agent tool: `category_delete`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Fields and labels (`field-overlays`), Active field (`active-field`), Filters (`filters`), Colors (`colors`), Highlights (`highlights`), Views (`views`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A categorical column of the cells by name (source "obs"). |
| `category` | string | yes | A category label as the legend shows it. Not empty. |
| `unassigned_label` | string | no | The category the cells move into, made when missing. Not empty. Default `"Unassigned"`. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"category":"T cells"}
```

Timeline label: Deleted the category T cells of cell_type

Pseudocode: `delete_category("cell_type", "T cells")`

### `category.merge`

**Merge two categories.** Move every cell of one category into another. The merged category is named "merged <category> + <into>" (as the legend's drag names it) unless label names it: give label the into category's own name to keep it. A column from the file becomes a new column (the original moves to Deleted fields); a column made in the app is edited in place.

- Agent tool: `category_merge`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)

| `category` | string | yes | The category whose cells move. Not empty. |
| `into` | string | yes | The category they join. Not empty. |
| `label` | string | no | The merged category's name; "merged &lt;category> + &lt;into>" when left out. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"category":"T cells","into":"B cells"}
```

Timeline label: Merged T cells into B cells in cell_type

Pseudocode: `merge_categories("cell_type", "T cells", into="B cells")`

### `field.consensus`

**Build the consensus column.** The community annotation's consensus for a categorical column as a column of its own: each cell gets the agreed label of its category, or the status of a category without one (disputed, pending); built again under the same name, it is replaced. The outcome of each category is named in the parameters, so it replays by name on any dataset with the same column and categories.

- Agent tool: `field_consensus`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Fields and labels (`field-overlays`), Active field (`active-field`), Filters (`filters`), Colors (`colors`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | The consensus column's name. Not empty. |
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | The annotated column the consensus is of. |
| `mapping` | list of object (`category`, `status`, `label`, `voters`) | yes | The outcome of each category of the column (a category left out is pending). At least 1 item. |
| `settings` | object (`minAnnotators`, `threshold`) | yes | The consensus rule it was built with. |
| `provenance` | object (`repository`, `branch`, `commit`, `pulledAt`) | yes | Where the votes came from. |

Example:

```json
{"key":"x","field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"mapping":[{"category":"T cells","status":"consensus","label":"x","voters":0}],"settings":{"minAnnotators":0,"threshold":-1},"provenance":{"repository":"x","branch":"x","commit":"x","pulledAt":"x"}}
```

Timeline label: Built the consensus column x of cell_type

Pseudocode: `consensus_column("x", of="cell_type", mapping={"T cells": "x"})`

### `field.create-from-pages`

**Make a field from highlight pages.** A new categorical column whose categories are highlight pages, shown at once: each page's cells take its label; cells on several pages follow the overlap rule; cells on none keep their category of rest when it is given (refine an annotation: a page per new label, every other cell keeps its label), else take uncovered_label, a category only when there are such cells.

- Agent tool: `field_create_from_pages`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Fields and labels (`field-overlays`), Active field (`active-field`), Colors (`colors`)
- Depends on: Highlights (`highlights`), Open cells (`cells`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | The new column's name. Not empty. |
| `pages` | list of object (`page`, `label`) | yes | The pages, in order (first and last refer to it), each with its category label. At least 1 item. |
| `rest` | object (`source`, `key`) | no | A categorical column whose category the cells on no page keep (split one label: a page per new label, every other cell keeps its label in one call). A page label that is one of its categories is that category. |
| `uncovered_label` | string | no | The category of cells on no page (with rest: of those with no category there); empty leaves them without one. Default `"Unassigned"`. |
| `overlap` | one of `"first"`, `"last"`, `"overlap-label"`, `"intersections"` | no | Cells on several pages: the first page's label, the last's, the overlap label, or one label per combination of pages. Default `"first"`. |
| `overlap_label` | string | no | The label of cells on several pages when overlap is "overlap-label". Default `"Overlap"`. |
| `intersection_labels` | list of object (`pages`, `label`) | no | With overlap "intersections": the label of each combination of pages that has cells. Default `[]`. |

Example:

```json
{"key":"x","pages":[{"page":"x","label":"T cells"}]}
```

Timeline label: Made x from 1 highlight page

Pseudocode: `field_from_pages("x", {"x": "T cells"})`

## Data

### `cells.open`

**Open a share of the cells.** Read the dataset again with every cell, or with a subsample: an exact `count` of cells or a `fraction` of them, chosen by a subsample method; highlights, labels, views and filters are kept for the cells still open.

- Agent tool: `cells_open`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Open cells (`cells`), Data mapping (`mapping`), Expression values (`expression`), Fields and labels (`field-overlays`), Gene sets (`gene-sets`), Views (`views`), Active field (`active-field`), Filters (`filters`), Colors (`colors`), Hidden cells (`visibility`), Highlights (`highlights`), Camera (`camera`), Settings (`settings`), Analysis (`analysis`)
- A newer one replaces one still running

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | one of `"all"`, `"subsample"` | yes | all: every cell; subsample: the count or fraction given. |
| `count` | integer | no | How many cells, exactly (at least 2; the dataset's count or more opens every cell). Not with fraction. At least 1. |
| `fraction` | number | no | The share of the dataset's cells: 0.1 opens a tenth, 1 every cell. Not with count. More than 0, at most 1. |
| `method` | one of `"uniform"`, `"blocks"`, `"stratified"`, `"spatial"`, `null` | no | How the cells are chosen; null for the file's default. Default `null`. |
| `seed` | integer or null | no | The subsample's seed; null for the file's. At least 0, at most 4294967295. Default `null`. |
| `field` | string | no | Stratified: the categorical column it is stratified by. Not empty. |
| `allocation` | one of `"proportional"`, `"balanced"` | no | Stratified: how the cells are split over the categories. Default `"proportional"`. |
| `embedding` | string | no | Spatial: the obsm embedding it thins. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"mode":"all"}
```

Timeline label: Opened every cell

Pseudocode: `open_cells("all")`

### `cells.read-genes`

**Read genes for more cells.** Read every gene for the first `cells` open cells (a dataset stored cell by cell reads genes for a sample of the open cells); stopping keeps what was read.

- Agent tool: `cells_read_genes`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Open cells (`cells`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cells` | integer | yes | How many of the open cells; more than are open reads every one. At least 1. |

Example:

```json
{"cells":1}
```

Timeline label: Read genes for 1 cell

Pseudocode: `read_genes_for(1)`

### `expression.transform.set`

**Set the expression values.** Show and analyze the genes normalized to 10,000 counts per cell and/or log1p (Data mapping › Expression values; scanpy normalize_total(target_sum=1e4) then log1p). One setting for coloring, legends, filters, the cell card, reads and every analysis (pseudobulk differential expression always sums raw counts). The person's setting: an agent changes it only when the person asks. Offered when the mapped matrix holds counts; normalizing reads each cell's total from an obs column, else sums every gene once (heavy on a large matrix: asked first).

- Agent tool: `expression_transform_set`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Expression values (`expression`), Filters (`filters`), Colors (`colors`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `normalize` | boolean | no | Each cell's values scaled to 10,000 counts: x · 10,000 / the cell's total. |
| `log1p` | boolean | no | ln(1 + x), after the normalization when both are on. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

Timeline label: Expression values: as stored

Pseudocode: `set_expression_transform()`

### `mapping.set`

**Change the data mapping.** Choose which stored arrays are the embeddings, neighbor graph, genes (modality, expression matrix, gene names, log1p, highly variable), latent space and vector fields; groups not named stay as they are, except the genes groups, which follow a named modality (its defaults) or expression matrix (a gene-name or highly variable column its var axis has is kept, else its default), as the panel does. Applied as one change: refused, nothing changes.

- Agent tool: `mapping_set`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Data mapping (`mapping`), Views (`views`), Active field (`active-field`), Filters (`filters`), Colors (`colors`), Camera (`camera`), Analysis (`analysis`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `embeddings` | object (`enabled`, `defaults`) | no | The embeddings views can show, sorted by key then columns, and the default of each dimension. |
| `knn` | string or null | no | The obsp neighbor graph, or null for none. Not empty. |
| `modality` | string | no | The modality genes are read from (a dataset of several). Not empty. |
| `gene_names` | string | no | "index", or "column:&lt;var column>". Not empty. |
| `expression` | string or null | no | "X", "raw", "layer:&lt;name>", or null for no genes. Not empty. |
| `log1p` | list of object (`matrix`, `base`) | no | Each expression matrix that holds log1p values, with its base (null: e). |
| `highly_variable` | string or null | no | The boolean var column marking highly variable genes, or null. Not empty. |
| `latent` | string or null | no | The obsm latent space outlier filters use, or null. Not empty. |
| `vector_fields` | list of object (`key`, `embedding`) | no | Vector fields bound to enabled embeddings, sorted by embedding then key. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

Timeline label: Applied the data mapping

Pseudocode: `set_data_mapping()`

## Highlights

### `highlight.category`

**Highlight categories.** Add the cells of one or more categories of a field, as the selected view shows them, each category as a group of its own, in one step.

- Agent tool: `highlight_category`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Highlights (`highlights`)
- Depends on: Open cells (`cells`), Data mapping (`mapping`), Expression values (`expression`), Fields and labels (`field-overlays`), Filters (`filters`), Hidden cells (`visibility`), Views (`views`)
- Run again on a stale step (the State panel) brings its result up to date

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A categorical field, by name. |
| `categories` | list of string | yes | The categories, by their labels as the legend shows them: each becomes a group of the page, all in one step. One already on the page is brought up to the cells the view shows now. At least 1 item, each once. |
| `page` | string | no | The page the group goes on, by name; a page of that name is made when there is none. Omitted: the page shown, or with `color`, a page of that color. Not empty. |
| `color` | string | no | The color of the page the group goes on. With `page`, the color of the page made (an existing page must already have it). Without, the page shown when it has this color, else the first page that has it, else a new page of it. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"categories":["T cells"]}
```

Timeline label: Highlighted "T cells" of cell_type

Pseudocode: `highlight_category("cell_type", ["T cells"])`

### `highlight.cells`

**Highlight cells.** Add a group of cells to a highlight page: a confirmed selection, or cells an agent or notebook names.

- Agent tool: `highlight_cells`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Highlights (`highlights`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cells` | cells (original positions) | yes | Cells by original position, each once, in any order: the 0-based row of obs in the order the data was given. A file prepare() wrote holds its rows in priority order, so a row of it read as stored is not that position: its obs["cellucid_original_position"] gives the row's (or pass obs names). At least 1 item. |
| `label` | string | no | The group's label; omitted, "Highlight" (the list shows its cell count). A label already on the page gets " (2)", " (3)", …. Not empty. |
| `tool` | one of `"annotation"`, `"lasso"`, `"proximity"`, `"knn"` | no | The selection tool that made the cells (annotation for cells named directly). Default `"annotation"`. |
| `page` | string | no | The page the group goes on, by name; a page of that name is made when there is none. Omitted: the page shown, or with `color`, a page of that color. Not empty. |
| `color` | string | no | The color of the page the group goes on. With `page`, the color of the page made (an existing page must already have it). Without, the page shown when it has this color, else the first page that has it, else a new page of it. |

Example:

```json
{"cells":[0,1,2]}
```

Timeline label: Highlighted 3 cells

Pseudocode: `highlight_cells(<3 cells>)`

### `view.picture`

**Take a picture of a view.** A PNG of a view as the figure export draws it (points, legend), or as the screen shows it now (source "screen": the vector field overlay, the connectivity edges and a playing camera path's caption included, which a figure cannot draw), or the whole figure exactly as Export would download it now with the Figure export settings (source "export": size, frame, background, fonts, title, panel titles, legends, every view while Export all views is on: check a figure with it before the person downloads it); returned as base64; nothing is downloaded.

- Agent tool: `view_picture`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | string | no | The view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers it; the selected view when left out. Not with source "export" (it draws what Export would). |
| `source` | one of `"figure"`, `"screen"`, `"export"` | no | figure: one view drawn as the figure export draws it (points, legend; no overlay), with plain settings (no title, 12 px text, the screen's background). screen: the view's pane as the screen shows it now, overlays included (the moving flow caught at this instant), no legend; the view must be on screen. export: the figure Export would download now, with every Figure export setting (figure_export_set), scaled down into width × height (ask 1200 × 1200 or more to read a multi-panel figure's titles). Default `"figure"`. |
| `width` | integer | no | The width of the box the plot fits in, in pixels: the plot keeps the view's shape inside width × height, as the figure export frames it (the picture adds its margins and the legend). With source "export": the box the whole figure is scaled down into (never up). At least 100, at most 20000. Default `640`. |
| `height` | integer | no | The height of the box the plot fits in, in pixels (source "export": of the box the figure is scaled into). At least 100, at most 20000. Default `480`. |
| `legend` | boolean | no | Draw the color legend beside the plot (a figure picture; the screen has none). Default `true`. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `png` | string | The image, base64-encoded PNG bytes (an agent receives it as an image). |
| `width` | integer | The image's width in pixels. |
| `height` | integer | The image's height in pixels. |
| `plot` | object (`width`, `height`) or null | The plot's size in the image: the largest rectangle of the view's shape inside the width × height asked for; null for an "export" picture of every view. |
| `view` | string or null | The view drawn, by its name; null for an "export" picture of every view. |
| `label` | string or null | The name the view was given (view_rename), or null. |
| `notes` | list of string | What the picture leaves out of what the view shows, or draws over it (a figure: an overlay it cannot draw; the screen: the legend; both: the highlighted cells drawn in the highlight's color over the coloring); for "export", first the figure's own size. |

## Camera

### `camera.framing`

**Frame cells with the camera.** Where cells sit in a view and cameras that frame them, seen from a direction: the whole view, each category of a field (or those named), and those named together. Nothing moves; give a camera to camera_set or camera_path_keyframe_add. It frames the view as it is laid out now (side by side, a view is narrower): arrange the views first.

- Agent tool: `camera_framing`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | string | no | The view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers it; the selected view when left out. |
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | no | A categorical field whose categories to frame, each on its own. |
| `categories` | list of string | no | Only these categories of the field; they are also framed together. Omitted, every category the view shows. At least 1 item, each once. |
| `azimuth` | number | no | Degrees around the vertical axis the camera looks from (3D views); omitted, the view's own. 90 apart is a quarter turn. |
| `elevation` | number | no | Degrees above (positive) or below the subject the camera looks from (3D views); omitted, the view's own. At least -85, at most 85. |
| `fill` | number | no | How much of the frame the cells fill across or up: 0.8 a close shot with a margin, 0.4 the subject with its surroundings. More than 0, at most 1. Default `0.8`. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `view` | string |  |
| `embedding` | object (`name`, `dimension`) or null |  |
| `navigation` | one of `"orbit"`, `"planar"` | The mode of the cameras: orbit for 3D, planar (facing the x–y plane) for 1D and 2D. |
| `direction` | object (`azimuth`, `elevation`) or null |  |
| `frame` | object (`aspect`, `vertical_view_degrees`, `fill`) |  |
| `whole` | object (`cells`, `center`, `extent`, `camera`, `foreground`, `nearest`) |  |
| `together` | object (`cells`, `center`, `extent`, `camera`, `foreground`, `nearest`) | The categories named, in one shot. |
| `field` | string |  |
| `groups` | list of object (`label`, `cells`, `center`, `extent`, `camera`, `foreground`, `nearest`) |  |
| `not_shown` | list of string | Categories with no cell the view shows (filtered or hidden). |

### `camera.navigation.set`

**Set the navigation mode.** Navigate a view by orbit, planar or free-fly (O, P and G); views with linked cameras share one mode.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |

| `view` | string | yes | A view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers its rows (the live view is View 1 while it is shown, the kept views follow in the order they were kept). |
| `mode` | one of `"orbit"`, `"planar"`, `"free"` | yes | "orbit", "planar" or "free" (free-fly). |

Example:

```json
{"view":"View 1","mode":"orbit"}
```

Timeline label: Navigated View 1 by orbit

Pseudocode: `set_navigation_mode("View 1", "orbit")`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

### `camera.set`

**Place the camera.** Set the camera of a view (views with linked cameras follow); a camera gesture records one of these.

- Agent tool: `camera_set`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Camera (`camera`)
- Repeated at once (a drag, a gesture), it is one step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | string | yes | A view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers its rows (the live view is View 1 while it is shown, the kept views follow in the order they were kept). |
| `camera` | object (`navigationMode`, `orbit`, `freefly`) | yes | A camera: its navigation mode, and its orbit and free-fly poses (the one the mode drives is used). Coordinates are the view's (the embedding scaled to about -1..1, y up); an orbit camera sits at target + radius·(sin phi·cos theta, cos phi, sin phi·sin theta) looking at target (theta the azimuth, phi from straight above, radians); a planar one at target + (0, 0, radius). Take cameras from `camera_framing` rather than composing them. |

Example:

```json
{"view":"View 1","camera":{"navigationMode":"orbit","orbit":{"radius":1,"targetRadius":1,"theta":0,"phi":0,"target":[0,0,0]},"freefly":{"position":[0,0,0],"yaw":0,"pitch":0}}}
```

Timeline label: Moved the camera of View 1

Pseudocode: `set_camera("View 1", <camera>)`

```json
{}
```

| `return_to_start` | boolean | Ends with a return to the first keyframe. |

**Set a camera path hold.** Set how long the camera rests at one keyframe, or at every keyframe, before moving on (0 for no rest). The path grows by the hold; each transition keeps its time.


### `camera-path.keyframe.add`

**Add a camera path keyframe.** Save a camera as the next keyframe of the camera path (before the return to start, when there is one), optionally with a hold: seconds the camera rests there.

- Agent tool: `camera_path_keyframe_add`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Camera path (`camera-path`)
- Depends on: Camera (`camera`)
- Holds what it read of Camera (`camera`): a later change of it never makes the step stale

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `camera` | object (`navigationMode`, `orbit`, `freefly`) | no | The camera to save, whole (one from camera_framing or views_state); omitted, the selected view's camera now. |
| `label` | string | no | The keyframe's label, the shot's name: in the Camera path list, and, while the path plays with captions on (the default), its caption over the plot from halfway into the move to it until halfway out of it, as a documentary's title ("Beta cells", "Overview"; short, a title case phrase). Omitted, "KF n", which is never captioned. Unique among the keyframes. Not empty. |
| `embedding` | object (`key`, `columns`) or null | no | The embedding the keyframe was recorded on; omitted, the one the selected view shows. |
| `hold` | number | no | Seconds the camera rests at the keyframe before moving on; omitted, 0 (none). At least 0. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

Timeline label: Saved camera path keyframe "new"

Pseudocode: `add_keyframe()`

| `direction` | one of `"up"`, `"down"` | yes | "up" one place earlier, "down" one place later. |

Example:

```json
{"keyframe":"x","direction":"up"}
```

Timeline label: Moved camera path keyframe "x" earlier

Pseudocode: `move_keyframe("x", "up")`

### `camera-path.loop-back.set`

**End the camera path at its start.** Add or remove a last keyframe that returns the camera to the first one (two keyframes or more).

- Agent tool: `camera_path_loop_back_set`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Camera path (`camera-path`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | true to end with the return, false to remove it. |

Example:

```json
{"enabled":false}
```

Timeline label: Removed the camera path's return to its start

Pseudocode: `set_keyframe_loop_back(False)`

### `camera-path.play`

**Play the camera path.** Play the camera path in the selected view from its first keyframe, as Play does; answers when it ends or camera_path_stop or the person's Stop stops it (the camera stays where it stopped; a looping path plays on until stopped, by camera_path_stop or the person's Stop of this turn), with ended "end", "stopped", "looping" or "reduced-motion": the person's system asks for reduced motion, so the camera went to the last keyframe without moving (seconds: how long it moved, 0 when at once); nothing played, so never describe a film that ran.

- Agent tool: `camera_path_play`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Camera (`camera`)
- Depends on: Camera path (`camera-path`)
- Holds what it read of Camera path (`camera-path`): a later change of it never makes the step stale
- Stopped (the person's Stop of an agent), it keeps what it did, as its step records

It takes no parameters.

Example:

```json
{}
```

Timeline label: Played the camera path

Pseudocode: `play_camera_path()`

### `camera-path.playback.set`

**Set camera path playback.** Set how the camera path plays: interpolation, easing, speed of automatic transitions, loop, autoplay and captions.

- Agent tool: `camera_path_playback_set`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Camera path (`camera-path`)
- Repeated at once (a drag, a gesture), it is one step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position_interpolation` | one of `"catmull-rom"`, `"linear"`, `"bezier"` | no | How positions between keyframes are drawn: catmull-rom is the smooth one (no jolt or overshoot at a keyframe; a keyframe repeated is a hold). |
| `rotation_interpolation` | one of `"slerp"`, `"linear"` | no | How the view direction turns between keyframes. |
| `easing` | one of `"linear"`, `"ease-in-out"`, `"ease-in"`, `"ease-out"` | no | How the path starts and ends: from rest and to rest (ease-in-out), from rest (ease-in), to rest (ease-out), or moving (linear); every transition keeps its own time. |
| `speed` | integer | no | Speed of automatic transitions, 1 (very slow) to 100 (very fast). At least 1, at most 100. |
| `loop` | boolean | no | Play the path again from its start when it ends. |
| `autoplay` | boolean | no | Start playing as soon as the path has two keyframes. |
| `captions` | boolean | no | Show each named keyframe's label as a caption over the plot while the path plays (on by default; a keyframe still called "KF n" has none). |

Example:

```json
{}
```

Timeline label: Set camera path playback: unchanged

Pseudocode: `set_camera_path_playback()`

### `camera-path.stop`

**Stop the camera path.** Stop a playing camera path where the camera is, at once, also while camera_path_play is still waiting for it to end (that play then answers ended "stopped", and its step holds the camera where it stopped).

- Agent tool: `camera_path_stop`
- Effect: `control`: it stops work under way (a playing camera path, a running analysis) at once, never waiting behind it; the work's own step records what it changed, so this records no step

It takes no parameters.

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `stopped` | boolean | False when no camera path was playing. |

Timeline label: Stopped the camera path

Pseudocode: `stop_camera_path()`

## Settings

### `figure-export.get`

**Read the figure export settings.** The Figure export panel's settings now, each named as figure-export.set names it: what Export would write, and what a session or the history put back.

- Agent tool: `figure_export_get`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

It takes no parameters.

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `size_preset` | one of `"single-column"`, `"one-and-half-column"`, `"double-column"`, `"custom"` | The figure's width as a journal column: single-column (89 mm), one-and-half-column (120 mm), double-column (183 mm); custom is the width given. A preset sets width. |
| `width` | number | The figure's width in millimetres; the figure is exactly this wide, at every resolution, and as tall as its plots make it (each keeps its view's shape, or its frame's: set a frame to change the shape). A width that is not a preset's makes size_preset custom. At least 10. |
| `frame` | object (`lock_aspect`, `rect`) or null | The part of the view exported (needs the preview on), or null for the whole view. |
| `background` | one of `"viewer"`, `"white"`, `"transparent"`, `"custom"` | The background: the viewer's, white, transparent or custom. |
| `background_color` | string | The custom background color, lowercase #rrggbb. |
| `font_family` | one of `"Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif"`, `"Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"`, `"\"Times New Roman\", Times, serif"` | The font of every text. |
| `auto_text_size` | boolean | Set the text in the sizes journals print figure text at: 7 pt, ticks and centroid labels 6 pt, the title 8 pt (font_sizes is then null). |
| `font_sizes` | object (`base`, `legend`, `ticks`, `axis_label`, `title`, `centroid_label`) or null | Text sizes in points (1/72 inch; halves allowed) while auto_text_size is off, else null. They keep their printed size at any width and resolution. |
| `title_follows_dataset` | boolean | The title is the dataset's name (title is then null). |
| `title` | string or null | The figure title while it does not follow the dataset, else null. |
| `x_label` | string | The x axis label. |
| `y_label` | string | The y axis label. |
| `include_axes` | boolean | Draw the axes. |
| `include_legend` | boolean | Draw the legend. |
| `reference_grid` | boolean | Draw a reference grid. |
| `show_orientation` | boolean | Draw the 3D orientation indicator. |
| `depth_sort` | boolean | Draw 3D points back to front. |
| `legend_position` | one of `"right"`, `"bottom"` | Where the legend goes. |
| `emphasize_selection` | boolean | Fade the cells that are not highlighted. |
| `selection_muted_opacity` | number | The opacity of the faded cells, 0 to 1. At least 0, at most 1. |
| `preview` | object (`enabled`, `colorblind_mode`) | The preview in the panel and the color-vision deficiency it simulates; with the preview on, view.picture with source "export" draws that simulation too (Export writes the true colors). |
| `download` | one of `"svg"`, `"png"`, `"svg+png"`, `"png-multi"`, `"all"` | What Export downloads. |
| `dpi` | one of `150`, `300`, `600` | The resolution of a PNG: its pixels are the width in inches times this (an SVG is the same size, as vectors). |
| `svg_strategy` | one of `"full-vector"`, `"optimized-vector"`, `"hybrid"` | How an SVG draws its points: full-vector (the default: every point a circle, editable; a file grows with the cells drawn), optimized-vector (fewer points, optimized_target_count), hybrid (the points as one image, text and axes as vector: small at any cell count). |
| `optimized_target_count` | integer | How many points an optimized SVG keeps. At least 1000, at most 5000000. |
| `export_all_views` | boolean | Export every view of the multiview, side by side: each panel is titled by its view's name (view_rename; a view with none by its field and filters). |

### `figure-export.set`

**Change figure export settings.** Set Figure export options: width (millimetres or a journal column; the figure fills it, text in points keeps its printed size), frame (frame "cells" fits it to the cells, so plots take their shape, not the pane's), background, fonts, title and axis labels, axes, legend, preview, what Export downloads; only those given change, nothing is exported (figure-export.get reads them; view.picture with source "export" shows the figure they make).

- Agent tool: `figure_export_set`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Settings (`settings`)
- Repeated at once (a drag, a gesture), it is one step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size_preset` | one of `"single-column"`, `"one-and-half-column"`, `"double-column"`, `"custom"` | no | The figure's width as a journal column: single-column (89 mm), one-and-half-column (120 mm), double-column (183 mm); custom is the width given. A preset sets width. |
| `width` | number | no | The figure's width in millimetres; the figure is exactly this wide, at every resolution, and as tall as its plots make it (each keeps its view's shape, or its frame's: set a frame to change the shape). A width that is not a preset's makes size_preset custom. At least 10. |
| `frame` | object (`lock_aspect`, `rect`) or null or `"cells"` | no | The part of the view exported (needs the preview on, which "cells" turns on), null for the whole view, or "cells": the frame every cell the figure draws fills, with a small margin (the panel's Fit the cells), so a plot takes the cells' shape instead of its pane's (a narrow pane gives a narrow plot; never rearrange the person's screen for a figure). With export_all_views, one frame holding every panel's cells. |
| `background` | one of `"viewer"`, `"white"`, `"transparent"`, `"custom"` | no | The background: the viewer's, white, transparent or custom. |
| `background_color` | string | no | The custom background color, lowercase #rrggbb. |
| `font_family` | one of `"Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif"`, `"Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"`, `"\"Times New Roman\", Times, serif"` | no | The font of every text. |
| `auto_text_size` | boolean | no | Set the text in the sizes journals print figure text at: 7 pt, ticks and centroid labels 6 pt, the title 8 pt (font_sizes is then null). |
| `font_sizes` | object (`base`, `legend`, `ticks`, `axis_label`, `title`, `centroid_label`) or null | no | Text sizes in points (1/72 inch; halves allowed) while auto_text_size is off, else null. They keep their printed size at any width and resolution. |
| `title_follows_dataset` | boolean | no | The title is the dataset's name (title is then null). |
| `title` | string or null | no | The figure title while it does not follow the dataset, else null. |
| `x_label` | string | no | The x axis label. |
| `y_label` | string | no | The y axis label. |
| `include_axes` | boolean | no | Draw the axes. |
| `include_legend` | boolean | no | Draw the legend. |
| `reference_grid` | boolean | no | Draw a reference grid. |
| `show_orientation` | boolean | no | Draw the 3D orientation indicator. |
| `depth_sort` | boolean | no | Draw 3D points back to front. |
| `legend_position` | one of `"right"`, `"bottom"` | no | Where the legend goes. |
| `emphasize_selection` | boolean | no | Fade the cells that are not highlighted. |
| `selection_muted_opacity` | number | no | The opacity of the faded cells, 0 to 1. At least 0, at most 1. |
| `preview` | object (`enabled`, `colorblind_mode`) | no | The preview in the panel and the color-vision deficiency it simulates; with the preview on, view.picture with source "export" draws that simulation too (Export writes the true colors). |
| `download` | one of `"svg"`, `"png"`, `"svg+png"`, `"png-multi"`, `"all"` | no | What Export downloads. |
| `dpi` | one of `150`, `300`, `600` | no | The resolution of a PNG: its pixels are the width in inches times this (an SVG is the same size, as vectors). |
| `svg_strategy` | one of `"full-vector"`, `"optimized-vector"`, `"hybrid"` | no | How an SVG draws its points: full-vector (the default: every point a circle, editable; a file grows with the cells drawn), optimized-vector (fewer points, optimized_target_count), hybrid (the points as one image, text and axes as vector: small at any cell count). |
| `optimized_target_count` | integer | no | How many points an optimized SVG keeps. At least 1000, at most 5000000. |
| `export_all_views` | boolean | no | Export every view of the multiview, side by side: each panel is titled by its view's name (view_rename; a view with none by its field and filters). |

Example:

```json
{"size_preset":"double-column","include_axes":false}
```

Timeline label: Figure export: size preset double-column, include axes off

Pseudocode: `set_figure_export(size_preset="double-column", include_axes=false)`

### `field.categories`

**Read the categories of a field.** Each category of a categorical field with its cells, the cells shown in the active view, its color and whether it is shown.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"}}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `field` | string |  |
| `view` | string | The view the colors and shown counts are of (the selected one), named as actions name views ("View N"). |

### `field.summary`

**Summarize a field per category.** A continuous field or a gene per category of a categorical field (cells, mean, median, range, share above zero), or a categorical field's top categories per category.

- Agent tool: `field_summary`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A field by name: source "obs" for a column of the cells, "var" for a gene; key is the name as shown. |
| `by` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | The categorical obs field to group the cells by. |
| `categories` | list of string | no | Only these categories of `by`, by name (else every category with cells). At least 1 item, each once. |
| `top` | integer | no | For a categorical field: at most this many of its categories per group. At least 1. Default `50`. |
| `visible_only` | boolean | no | Only the cells the active view shows. Default `false`. |
| `within` | object (`field`, `categories`, `min`, `max`) | no | Only the cells of some categories of another categorical field, or in a range of a continuous field or gene (both ends included), leaving the view as it is: donors within one cell type, cell types per age range. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"by":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"}}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`, `kind`) |  |
| `by` | string |  |
| `within` | object (`field`, `cells`) or null | The cells kept by `within`: its field and how many open cells it keeps; null without it. |
| `values` | string or null | For a gene: its values as shown and analyzed (Data mapping › Expression values, expression_transform_set): raw counts as stored, or the transform and where the cells' totals came from; null for an obs field. |
| `empty` | integer | Categories of `by` left out for having no cells (none open, or none the view shows). At least 0. |
| `read_for` | object (`cells`, `of`) or null | For a gene read for a sample of the open cells: the cells its statistics are of. |
| `groups` | list of object (`label`, `cells`, `mean`, `median`, `min`, `max`, `above_zero`, `top`) |  |

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

| `query` | string | no | Only fields whose key contains this text (any case). Not empty. |

```json
{}
```

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fields` | list of object (`key`, `kind`, `categories`, `user_defined`) |  |

### `genes.search`

**Search the genes.** Gene names matching what is typed, best first, as the gene search box ranks them; or, given names, which of them the dataset has.

- Agent tool: `genes_search`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | no | What is typed (give it or names). Not empty. |
| `names` | list of string | no | Gene names to look up at once, exact in any case: genes lists those the dataset has, as it names them; lacks the rest. At least 1 item. |
| `limit` | integer | no | At most this many names (for a query). At least 1. Default `20`. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `genes` | list of string |  |
| `matches` | integer | How many genes match in all. At least 0. |
| `total` | integer | How many genes the dataset has. At least 0. |
| `lacks` | list of string | Of the names asked for, those that are not genes of the dataset. |

### `vector-field.summary`

**Summarize where cells are heading.** Where the cells of each category of a field are heading along a vector field (RNA velocity, a drift), in the embedding a view shows: per category, how fast (mean speed relative to the mean cell), how aligned its arrows are, their mean direction in the view's axes, and the categories its arrows lead into (each cell's arrow shared among its nearest cells by how directly it points at them, as scVelo's velocity graph does, here in the embedding). Read from the arrows as drawn in that embedding, not from the genes: an embedding can bend, merge or reverse a flow.

- Agent tool: `vector_field_summary`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `by` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | The categorical field to group the cells by. |
| `vector_field` | string | no | The vector field, by name (dataset_summary lists them). Left out: the one the overlay shows, else the dataset's default, else the only one bound to the view's embedding; with several bound and none of those, name one. Not empty. |
| `view` | string | no | The view whose embedding the arrows are read in: "View N"; the selected view when left out. |
| `categories` | list of string | no | Only these categories of `by` (else every category with cells); their arrows still lead into every category. At least 1 item, each once. |
| `neighbors` | integer | no | How many nearest cells (in the embedding) each cell's arrow is shared among. At least 2. Default `30`. |
| `visible_only` | boolean | no | Only the cells the view shows (its filters and hidden categories), as cells and as neighbors. Default `false`. |

Example:

```json
{"by":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"}}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `vector_field` | string |  |
| `view` | string |  |
| `embedding` | object (`name`, `dimension`) |  |
| `by` | string |  |
| `cells` | integer | Cells read (with a vector and a category). At least 0. |
| `without_vector` | integer | Cells left out for having no vector. At least 0. |
| `neighbors` | integer | At least 0. |
| `empty` | integer | Categories left out for having no cells read. At least 0. |
| `groups` | list of object (`label`, `cells`, `speed`, `coherence`, `direction`, `heading`, `towards`) |  |

## Analysis

### `analysis.cancel`

**Stop an analysis.** Stop a running analysis, at once, also while its run is still waiting for it; what it was showing stays, nothing else changes.

- Agent tool: `analysis_cancel`
- Effect: `control`: it stops work under way (a playing camera path, a running analysis) at once, never waiting behind it; the work's own step records what it changed, so this records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `analysis` | one of `"markers"`, `"differential"`, `"dotplot"`, `"signature"`, `"composition"`, `"correlation"` | yes | An analysis with a Run button. |
| `in` | `"panel"` or integer | no | Default `"panel"`. |

Example:

```json
{"analysis":"markers"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `stopped` | boolean | False when it was not running. |

Pseudocode: `stop_analysis("markers")`

## Exports

### `analysis.export`

**Export an analysis result.** Write an analysis's whole result table as a CSV file, as its expanded view's CSV button does: differential expression every gene with scanpy's columns (scores, logfoldchanges, pvals, pvals_adj, pct_nz_group, pct_nz_reference, auroc, means, cells); marker genes the shown markers of each group, or with all every gene of every group; the dot plot one row per group and gene; gene signature every cell's score per set and page (per set and group with a Group by field); composition the results per cell type with a test, else the counts; correlation each page's statistics. Refused, saying why, when there is no result or it is out of date (run it again first).

- Agent tool: `analysis_export`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it writes a file (`writes-file`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `analysis` | one of `"markers"`, `"differential"`, `"dotplot"`, `"signature"`, `"composition"`, `"correlation"` | yes | An analysis with a Run button. |
| `in` | `"panel"` or integer | no | Default `"panel"`. |
| `all` | boolean | no | Marker genes only: every gene of every group (the All genes CSV) instead of the shown markers. Default `false`. |

Example:

```json
{"analysis":"markers"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `analysis` | string | The analysis exported. |
| `file` | string | The file written. |
| `bytes` | integer | At least 0. |

Timeline label: Exported the marker genes result as CSV

Pseudocode: `export_analysis("markers")`

## Datasets

### `dataset.open`

**Open a dataset.** Open a dataset by the name the person gives: a built-in sample, one of their datasets (My datasets), a link, or an accession the link box takes. It replaces the open dataset; that one's history stays kept in this browser while Autosave keeps it (steps it does not keep are asked about first) and the new one starts its own. A link, accession or server the person has not typed, pasted or opened in this tab is asked of them first (before anything is requested), and so is a whole-file download. A count or fraction opens that subsample of its cells at once, read once (as cells_open takes it); without, it opens with the cells the person chose for openings (Session › Subsampling), or the cells one of My datasets was last open with.

- Agent tool: `dataset_open`
- Effect: `dataset`: it opens another dataset, whose history starts anew (the open one's stays kept in this browser while Autosave keeps it), and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it downloads a lot (`large-download`)
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it while the dataset shown holds steps this browser is not keeping (Autosave off, no storage or no room), which it would drop (`replaces-unkept`)
- Asks the person first when an agent names a link, an accession or a server they have not seen in this tab, before anything of it is requested (`unseen-link`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | A sample's name or id, a name from My datasets, a link to a dataset (a file, a Zarr store, a dataset folder, a CELLxGENE, Zenodo, Figshare or GitHub address), an accession (GSE123456, a DOI), or a Cellucid server (localhost:8765). Not empty. |
| `kind` | one of `"any"`, `"sample"`, `"my-datasets"`, `"link"` | no | Where to look for the name: any (samples, then My datasets, then as a link), sample, my-datasets or link. Default `"any"`. |
| `count` | integer | no | How many cells, exactly (at least 2; the dataset's count or more opens every cell). Not with fraction. At least 1. |
| `fraction` | number | no | The share of the dataset's cells: 0.1 opens a tenth, 1 every cell. Not with count. More than 0, at most 1. |
| `method` | one of `"uniform"`, `"blocks"`, `"stratified"`, `"spatial"`, `null` | no | How the cells are chosen; null for the file's default. Default `null`. |
| `seed` | integer or null | no | The subsample's seed; null for the file's. At least 0, at most 4294967295. Default `null`. |
| `field` | string | no | Stratified: the categorical column it is stratified by. Not empty. |
| `allocation` | one of `"proportional"`, `"balanced"` | no | Stratified: how the cells are split over the categories. Default `"proportional"`. |
| `embedding` | string | no | Spatial: the obsm embedding it thins. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"name":"Pancreatic endocrinogenesis (scVelo)"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | The dataset now open, as Cellucid names it. |
| `kind` | one of `"sample"`, `"link"`, `"server"`, `"file"`, `"folder"`, `"notebook"` | Where it opens from: a built-in sample, a link, a Cellucid server, a file or folder of the person's computer, or a notebook (Python, R) that serves it. |
| `cells` | integer | The cells open (a share of the dataset when it is subsampled). At least 0. |
| `total_cells` | integer | At least 0. |
| `genes` | integer or null | At least 0. |
| `saved_states` | integer | Histories of this dataset kept in this browser from earlier visits; the person was offered to continue the latest. At least 0. |
| `already_open` | boolean | It was open already, so nothing was opened again and its history goes on. |

Timeline label: Opened Pancreatic endocrinogenesis (scVelo)

Pseudocode: `open_dataset("Pancreatic endocrinogenesis (scVelo)")`

## Community annotation

### `annotation.publish`

**Vote and suggest labels.** Vote suggested labels of categories up or down (none takes the person's vote back) and suggest new labels in the person's name (each with their upvote, as the voting dialog's New suggestion does), and publish all of them together as one commit: the person's own file in the community annotation repository is written as published now plus these changes (a pull request when they cannot write to the repository), which others see on their next Pull. Put everything of a turn in one call: each call is one commit of the person's file and one question to them. Nothing else of the person's is published; votes that change nothing publish nothing. A label already suggested for its category is refused with its id (vote on it instead), and nothing of a call is published when any of it is refused. Asked of the person first; the history cannot take it back. Refused until the person has connected the repository and signed in to GitHub.

- Agent tool: `annotation_publish`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it publishes (`publishes`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `votes` | list of object (`field`, `category`, `suggestion`, `vote`) | no | The votes, each on one suggestion of one category; one vote per suggestion. |
| `suggestions` | list of object (`field`, `category`, `label`, `ontology_id`, `evidence`) | no | The new labels, each for one category; one label once per category. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `repository` | string | The GitHub repository of the community annotation. |
| `published` | one of `"repository"`, `"pull-request"`, `"unchanged"` | Where the changes went, as one commit: written to the repository, in a pull request its authors merge, or nowhere (the votes were already so). |
| `pull_request` | string or null | The pull request, when they went to one. |
| `votes` | list of object (`category`, `suggestion`, `vote`, `up`, `down`) | Each vote, in the order given, with its suggestion's counts now. |
| `suggestions` | list of object (`category`, `id`, `label`) | Each suggestion, in the order given. |
| `not_published` | integer or null | The person's other changes still not published (null when not known). At least 0. |

Timeline label: Published nothing to the community annotation

Pseudocode: `annotation_publish()`

### `annotation.suggestions`

**Read the community annotation.** The labels suggested for the categories of a field by the community annotation of the dataset shown (its connected GitHub repository), with their votes, the person's own vote and each category's consensus, as the voting dialog and the legend show them; whether the field is open for voting, and when this browser last pulled. The repository is pulled first when this browser has not pulled it yet, or when asked (pull), as GitHub sync › Pull latest does: nothing of the person's is published. One page holds what fits a tool result; `next` starts the following one.

- Agent tool: `annotation_suggestions`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A categorical column of the cells by name (source "obs"). |
| `category` | string | no | One category; every category of the field when left out. Not empty. |
| `cursor` | integer | no | Where the page starts: the next of the last page; the first page when left out. At least 0. |
| `pull` | boolean | no | Pull the latest suggestions and votes from the repository first (true), or read what this browser has (false). Left out: pulled only when this browser has not pulled the repository yet. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"}}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `repository` | string | The GitHub repository it is kept in. |
| `pulled_at` | string or null | When this browser last pulled from it (an ISO instant), null before the first Pull: votes made since are not here. |
| `annotated` | boolean | The field is open to community annotation. |
| `closed` | boolean | Voting on the field is closed (only its authors still vote). |
| `consensus_rule` | object (`voters_needed`, `threshold`) or null | The repository's rule for the field, which each consensus follows: a category is pending until at least voters_needed people (and at least one) voted on any of its suggestions; then it is agreed when one label leads (labels rank by net votes, then by upvotes; equal on both is a tie, always disputed) and the leader's net share of the voters (up minus down, over the voters) is at least threshold, else disputed. Null when the repository sets none for the field. |
| `repository_field` | string | The field's name in the repository, when the person renamed it here. |
| `categories` | list of object (`category`, `repository_category`, `consensus`, `suggestions`) |  |
| `total_categories` | integer | Categories on every page. At least 0. |
